newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWB credits export monopoly for Pakistan premium.
newsitem.headline: AWB credits export monopoly for Pakistan premium.

text.p: Australia had extracted a price premium over the United States in its latest wheat sale to Pakistan because of the Australian Wheat Board's (AWB) export monopoly, a senior AWB executive said.

"That premium would not have been there if we were competing with a whole range of Australian producers," Nigel Officer, the AWB's general manager international, told an in-house conference being held in Melbourne.

The AWB faces a government review of its monopoly on export sales of Australian wheat in 1999 and is also under pressure from the United States, one of Australia's major competitors in global wheat markets, to abandon its single desk export powers.

Speaking with Reuters, Officer also said the sale made Pakistan one of Australia's major wheat markets this year. He said Pakistan was expected to continue to be a major importer of wheat and Australia was well-positioned to supply in 1997/98.

Officersaid the AWB was "pretty pleased" with its sales to Pakistan and with its prospects to continue to sell. The AWB's sale of 250,000 tonnes of wheat was priced at about US$158.00 a tonne, against less than $150.00 a tonne for the 200,000 tonnes sold by the United States and the 50,000 tonnes sold by Canada in the same tender.
The sale brought the AWB's sales of wheat from the 1996/97 crop to 1.35 million tonnes, well ahead of the less than 500,000 tonnes sold the year before.
